title: Platform-independent float maths: excali_math::js for every transcendental, std methods disallowed by clippy
description:
Upstream runs on V8, whose Math transcendentals are V8's own fdlibm on every OS, while Rust's f64 methods call the platform libm, which differs by an ulp between macOS and glibc. Port V8's code into excali_math::js, replace every std call, disallow the std methods in clippy.toml, run the test suite on macOS and Linux, and record the rule in an ADR and the architecture overview.

Evidence:
- ex-513: rotated bound text y = 247.5924092061952 on Linux against upstream's 247.59240920619527 (packages/excalidraw/tests/history.test.tsx:4396; glibc cos(90) is one ulp from V8's)
- V8 14.6.202.34 src/base/ieee754.cc (fdlibm), src/numbers/ieee754.cc math::pow (platform pow), src/builtins/math.tq MathHypot
- Node 26.10.0 arm64 against ieee754.cc built with clang -ffp-contract=on: equal on 400,000 random arguments per function (run 2026-09-28)
- tools/goldens/README.md: the goldens are the arm64 output; x86_64 V8 differs in the last bits
- https://crates.io/crates/pxfm 0.1.30 (BSD-3-Clause OR Apache-2.0; read 2026-09-28)
acceptance_criteria: excali_math::js ports V8's fdlibm (src/base/ieee754.cc, with the fused multiply-adds clang emits on arm64) for sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, exp, log, log2, log10 and cbrt, keeps V8's Math.hypot, and answers pow with V8's special cases and the correctly rounded power; goldens/js-math.json (tools/goldens/js-math.mjs, Node at tools/goldens/.node-version on arm64) and crates/excali-math/tests/js_math.rs pin V8's bits for special values, every reduction path and arguments where fdlibm without FMA or the platform's libm is an ulp away; every f64/f32 transcendental call in crates/** and tools/** goes through excali_math::js and the workspace clippy.toml disallows the std methods (clippy -D warnings); the rust workflow runs cargo test on ubuntu (x86_64 and arm64) and macOS with every golden, corpus and parity test green, the golden harness comparing exactly; excali-core and excali-math build for wasm32; ADR-011 and the architecture overview record the rule.
close_reason: excali_math::js ports V8's fdlibm (arm64 FMA) and correctly rounded pow; all transcendentals in crates/ and tools/ go through it; clippy.toml disallows std methods; tests on macOS and Linux (ADR-011)

title: Typed element model: keep field values of a type the model has no form for (string strokeWidth) as upstream's restore does
description:
ex-108 restores each library item's elements with upstream's restoreElements, then reads each restored object with Element::from_map. Upstream's restore copies a truthy strokeWidth as it is, so a string "3" survives and the element loads; the typed model reads numbers only, so the port drops the element. In the catalogue that loses the 24 lines of aarondiel/logic-gates. ex-114's round-trip acceptance still passes after the drop, so this task tracks it. The same rule applies to scenes read through restore. M1 cannot close while this data loss remains.

Evidence:

- fixtures/libraries: aarondiel/logic-gates holds 24 lines whose strokeWidth is the string "3"
- crates/excali-core/src/library.rs module docs (the two differences from upstream; Element::from_map rejects the object and restore drops the element)

title: excali-math js::sin/cos match V8's libm trig bit for bit; remove the 1e-12 tolerance in excali-editor tests/transform.rs
description:
ex-508's gesture fixtures come from upstream run in Node 26, whose V8 computes Math.sin/Math.cos with its glibc-derived routines, not fdlibm. excali_math::js ports fdlibm through the libm crate, which is one ulp away on some arguments, so a rotated element's numbers can differ in the last bits and ex-508's test compares numbers within a relative 1e-12. This task ports V8's trig routines so the port computes the same doubles and the tolerance goes.

Evidence:
- crates/excali-editor/tests/transform.rs same_number (relative tolerance 1e-12, introduced by ex-508)
- crates/excali-math/src/js.rs sin/cos (libm crate, fdlibm port)
- Node v26.10.0 on macOS arm64, 2026-09-28: node -e 'console.log(Math.cos(0.982953340331056))' prints 0.5545673797180782; fdlibm (libm crate) gives 0.5545673797180781
- V8 BUILD.gn v8_use_libm_trig_functions and third_party/glibc (sin/cos), src/base/ieee754.cc (atan2 still fdlibm)
acceptance_criteria: excali_math::js::sin and js::cos return the doubles Node 26 (V8 with v8_use_libm_trig_functions, glibc-derived sin/cos) returns, including Math.cos(0.982953340331056) = 0.5545673797180782 where fdlibm gives 0.5545673797180781, checked against a table of Node 26 answers in crates/excali-math/tests/js_trig.rs; same_number in crates/excali-editor/tests/transform.rs compares doubles exactly (a == e, -0 equal to 0) and every transform.json case passes; the goldens and export fixtures that go through js::sin/cos still pass.
notes: ex-009 (ADR-011, site/content/decisions/adr-011-platform-independent-float-maths.md): this task's premise is wrong. Node 26.10.0 builds V8 with gyp and tools/v8_gypfiles/features.gypi does not set v8_use_libm_trig_functions, so Node's Math.sin/Math.cos are V8's own fdlibm (src/base/ieee754.cc), not the glibc-derived routines; the ulp came from the libm crate lacking the fused multiply-adds clang emits on arm64. excali_math::js now ports ieee754.cc with those FMAs, and the acceptance value Math.cos(0.982953340331056) = 0.5545673797180782 is pinned in crates/excali-math/tests/js_math.rs:113 and passes through js::cos. What remains here is only removing the 1e-12 same_number tolerance in excali-editor tests/transform.rs once ex-508 and ex-009 are both on main.
